dedupe_keys.name: extremadura spain solar thermal domestic hot water in 25 hospitals investment and savings

description: This case study estimates what the 25 hospitals of Extremadura in western Spain could save by heating their domestic hot water with solar thermal energy. The authors, from the Engineering Projects Area of the University of Extremadura in Badajoz, studied hospitals between 533 and 87,118 square metres with 15 to 529 beds, simulated three solar fractions of 0.70, 0.75 and 0.80, and calculated the investment needed and the economic and environmental savings. The article was published in 2020 in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health and is free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Coverage is all hospitals of one Spanish region. Caveats: results are simulations with assumed costs and demand, not measured installations. A 70 percent solar contribution gave the best economic results and energy ratios, with an average payback of 4.74 years and 4.29 kilowatt hours per euro a year. An investment of 674,423 euros could generate 2,895,416 kilowatt hours a year of heat, saving 145,933 euros and 638 tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The authors recommend a 70 percent solar factor and prioritising hospitals in Cáceres over those in Badajoz, especially public ones with over 300 beds. Simulation uses: energy demand and on-site supply parameters for hospital energy resilience and investment models. Related records: the ASHE hospital energy benchmarking reports (data-ashe-hospital-energy-benchmarking-reports) and the hospital microgrid study (case_study-hospital-microgrid-reopt-grid-outage-resilience) address hospital energy.
